events.label: August jobs report (BLS, 8:30 AM ET) — consensus ~50-55K, unemployment 4.1%, average hourly earnings 3.0% YoY
events.note: Updated Sep 3 night: Waller's support for a September hold cut CME hike odds roughly 12 points to about 54.6%, so the print now lands into a tape already positioned for the dovish outcome — VIX 15.20 (-7%), 10Y 4.74%. Three labour signals point soft: ADP 38,000, ISM services employment 47.8 in contraction, continuing claims 1.78 million. That makes the hot print the asymmetric one: above 150,000 with firm average hourly earnings restores the odds Waller removed and puts the 10-year back through 4.818%. Near consensus with earnings at or under 0.3% confirms the hold and pushes the 10-year through 4.70%. Last major labour print before the Sep 15-16 FOMC.

events.label: Labor Day — US equity and bond markets closed
events.note: Cash markets shut for the session. Crypto and oil trade the weekend's Strait of Hormuz headlines unhedged, so a transit-suspension escalation over the long weekend gaps into Tuesday's open — eight days before the FOMC.

events.label: Canada retaliatory tariffs effective — dairy, appliances, ag equipment, pulp, paper, electronics
events.note: Updated Aug 28 night: Warsh's full Jackson Hole speech was hawkish — September hike odds rose to 59% from 33%. Warsh did not explicitly cite Canada tariff cost-push in the speech, leaving the tariff-inflation linkage as an open variable in the September 8-16 window. Tariffs arrive 4 days after the August jobs report (Sept 4) and 8 days before September 16 FOMC. With hike odds already at 59%, if hot jobs data and tariff cost-push both enter Fed communications between September 8 and 16, September hike odds above 65% are the two-variable scenario. DXY rose 0.4% to 99.50 on the Warsh hawkish signal — any tariff escalation that re-prices the dollar is the third input.

events.label: Oracle Q1 FY2027 results — first large AI-capex print since the Anthropic-Lambda deal
events.note: Carries a planned $20B equity issuance to fund AI infrastructure alongside the print. Read-through to how the market is pricing debt- and equity-funded datacenter buildout after Nvidia turned lessor on the $35B Lambda-Anthropic contract.

events.label: Bessent Treasury long-dated buyback ops begin — $4B+ per op, 10-20yr and 20-30yr bonds
events.note: Added Aug 19 night: Treasury Secretary Bessent announced August 19 the department will double the size of long-dated bond buyback operations, raising the maximum per-operation from $2B to at least $4B for bonds maturing in the 10-to-20-year and 20-to-30-year ranges. Effective September 9, runs through November 4 (end of current refunding quarter). The program provides structural demand support for the long end. If underlying supply dynamics overwhelm the $4B+ buyback, the 30Y could reassert above 5.25% before or during the program. BTC's structural debasement bid is partially underwritten by the buyback program as a signal of Treasury demand-management. Updated Sep 2 night: the 30Y closed near 5.26% in a fourth session inside 5.30%, having traded through the level twice without a close above it. The buyback bid arrives after Friday payrolls rather than before it, so the level is tested unsupported first.

events.label: August PPI (8:30 AM ET) — first of the two inflation prints Waller's hold is conditioned on
events.note: Added Sep 3 night: producer prices are where tariff and energy pass-through shows up before it reaches CPI, and they arrive two days after Canada's retaliatory tariffs take effect. ISM services prices paid at 72.6 and manufacturing prices at 71.1 argue the risk is to the upside. Waller said it 'may not take much acceleration in inflation' to move him back toward tightening, so this is the first of two prints that can undo the ~12-point repricing of September 3.

events.label: August CPI (8:30 AM ET) — the last inflation print before the FOMC, four trading days out
events.note: Added Sep 3 night: the print that resolves Waller's condition with no scheduled Fed communication left to soften it. Core CPI at or under 0.3% month over month keeps the hold intact; above 0.3% re-arms the hike inside four trading days of the September 15-16 decision, and would reverse the September 3 rally on the same mechanism that produced it.

events.label: FOMC decision (Sep 15-16) — September rate path; hike odds ~54.6% after Waller backed a hold
events.note: Updated Sep 3 night: Governor Waller told a Reuters event he would support holding — 'Give disinflation a chance. We can wait one meeting' — and CME September hike odds fell about 12 points to roughly 54.6%, still above even. The hold is explicitly conditional: policy is 'only slightly restricting aggregate demand' and 'it may not take much acceleration in inflation to nudge me into supporting tighter policy.' August PPI (Sep 10) and CPI (Sep 11) both resolve that condition before the decision, with ISM services prices paid at 72.6 and manufacturing prices at 71.1 arguing the risk is to the upside. Canada retaliatory tariffs (Sep 8) and Treasury long-dated buybacks (Sep 9) land inside the window. One governor is not the committee. Updated Sep 4 morning: the condition behind the hold moved against it over the week — WTI +10.4% and Brent +7.6% on Hormuz transit risk, with US average diesel prices at a record, arriving four trading days before the Sep 10 PPI print.

events.label: Bank of Japan policy decision — markets pricing a September hike after Deputy Governor Himino flagged upside inflation risks
events.note: Added Sep 4 morning: the yen reached 155.28 per dollar on Sep 3, its strongest in a month, on BOJ hike bets rather than on the Fed alone. The decision lands two days after the Sep 15-16 FOMC, so the funding currency behind a large share of global duration positioning reprices twice inside four sessions. A yen driven by Japanese tightening keeps appreciating on a hot US print as well as a soft one; USD/JPY back above 158 would say the BOJ leg was overstated.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — terminal insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut. Lock-up expiries are the known supply overhang for hot IPOs. Context after Aug 6-7: 20% first tranche absorbed at $105-$115; next tranches scheduled Aug 20 and late September. Q3 Starlink profitability (~October call) is the only fundamental catalyst that could revalue the lockup discount before the December terminal release. SPCX Q2: $18.37B capex vs $7.81B revenue; AI segment $2.56B (+247% YoY).

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). PLTR's 149% US commercial growth, AMD's $6.7B data-center (+107%), and SpaceX's exclusive Nvidia commitment ($15.83B AI capex) confirm the enterprise AI adoption underlying OpenAI's revenue model. NVDA circular financing disclosure ($250B OpenAI backstop) remains the unresolved structural question that may surface in S-1 filings.
